clue.text: Music setting worker on edge

indicators.note: in a down-style reading one piece placed on the other, here worker set before edge

parts.note: the ant is the crossword's standard worker insect
a hem is the folded edge of cloth

explanation.surface: A labourer is placed on a ledge to a backing of music.
explanation.definitionFit: A choral composition set to sacred or patriotic words is a musical setting of a text.

clue.text: Construction of neat run for an animal

indicators.note: a construction is something built up, so the letters of neat are assembled anew

parts.note: to lope is to run with a long easy stride

explanation.surface: Someone tidily building a run, a pen for some beast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Construction of' rearranges NEAT into ANTE, then LOPE (run) follows.
explanation.definitionFit: A swift horned grazing beast of Africa and Asia is a kind of animal.

clue.text: Jack's gratuities!

parts.note: gratuities are tips; the answer read as an instruction says turn the word SPIT round, which gives the tips

explanation.surface: Jack has done well out of tips.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as two words, the answer tells you to turn SPIT backwards, producing TIPS, the gratuities.
explanation.definitionFit: A jack is an old roasting device that rotates the spit, as was the kitchen boy who did that job.

clue.text: Always right behind the first mate

indicators.note: the abbreviation for right comes behind, after, the first mate

parts.note: Eve was Adam's partner, the first wife in Genesis

explanation.surface: Forever the right-hand man trailing the ship's first officer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'First mate' suggests a ship's officer; it is the Biblical Eve.
explanation.definitionFit: Ever means at all times, forever, as in 'ever faithful'.

clue.text: Make a song about the Left playing fair

indicators.note: the singing goes around, about, the left side

parts.note: to make a song is to sing
port is the left-hand side of a ship

explanation.surface: Kicking up a fuss about political leftists while claiming to be fair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The Left' looks political; it is PORT, the nautical left.
explanation.definitionFit: A sporting gesture is a fair, generous one, in keeping with good sportsmanship.

clue.text: Possibly getting into no tip-top race

indicators.note: possibly signals that the letters may be arranged otherwise

explanation.surface: Maybe not entering a first-rate contest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Possibly' rearranges INTO NO TIPTOP into the hyphenated answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A point-to-point is an amateur steeplechase for hunting horses, a British country race.

clue.text: Reckon on the traitor being given quarter

parts.note: a rat is someone who deserts or betrays his side
E, east, is one of the four quarters of the compass

explanation.surface: Counting on the turncoat being shown mercy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Given quarter' sounds like mercy; quarter is a compass point, E.
explanation.definitionFit: To rate something is to estimate or judge its value.

clue.text: A family of flowering plants — one climbs

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
rises means goes up, climbs

explanation.surface: A botanical group in which one species is a climber.
explanation.definitionFit: The iris family, Iridaceae, is a group of flowering bulbs and rhizomes, crocus and gladiolus among them.

clue.text: Unsophisticated egghead, a writer

parts.note: green means naive, inexperienced
the head of the word egg is its first letter E

explanation.surface: A naive intellectual who pens books.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Egghead' wants to be an intellectual; it is the head, first letter, of egg.
explanation.definitionFit: Graham Greene was the English novelist of Brighton Rock and The Power and the Glory.

clue.text: He painted a revolver

definitions.meaning: J M W ..., the English landscape artist

explanation.surface: An artist who carried a pistol.
explanation.definitionFit: J M W Turner was a celebrated English painter; literally, one who rotates something.

clue.text: Help backward ethnic group when there's much criticism

indicators.note: backward tells us to read the word for help from the end

parts.note: aid means help
a tribe is an ethnic group

explanation.surface: Aiding a disadvantaged people attracts heavy censure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Backward' turns AID into DIA before TRIBE.
explanation.definitionFit: A diatribe is a long bitter verbal attack, a torrent of criticism.

clue.text: Usual allowance for an American officer

parts.note: general means common, usual
a grant is a sum allowed or given

explanation.surface: The standard stipend paid to a US serviceman.
explanation.definitionFit: Ulysses S Grant commanded the Union armies in the Civil War, a famous US commander.

clue.text: Register the trainee first

parts.note: L stands for learner, as on a learner driver's plate
first is written 1st, and the figure 1 reads as the letter I

explanation.surface: Enrol the apprentice before anyone else.
explanation.walkthrough: First abbreviated is 1st; treating the numeral as the letter I gives IST.
explanation.definitionFit: A register is a roll of names, a catalogue or roster.

clue.text: Departure date is to be arranged by the month-end

indicators.note: by here means next to, so the final letter is placed alongside
the letters of the word date will be put in a fresh order

parts.note: the end of the word month is H

explanation.surface: A leaving date to be fixed by the end of the month.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Is to be arranged' turns DATE into DEAT; 'by' places the H from the end of month after it.
explanation.definitionFit: Death is the final departure, a euphemism for passing away.

clue.text: Persons occupied by a medium

indicators.note: the word for persons is filled by the letter A

parts.note: men are persons

explanation.surface: People possessed by a spirit-channeller at a seance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Medium' suggests a psychic; here it is an average.
explanation.definitionFit: A mean is the average, the middle value between extremes.

clue.text: Advance in early spring

definitions.meaning: the third month, when spring begins in the north

explanation.surface: Moving forward as the season turns.
explanation.definitionFit: Troops move forward on a route; the month comes at the start of the northern spring.

clue.text: The ploughman homeward plods his way" (Gray's Elegy)

definitions.text: The ploughman homeward plods his way" (Gray's Elegy)

parts.words: The ploughman homeward plods his way" (Gray's Elegy)
parts.note: a line from Thomas Gray's Elegy Written in a Country Churchyard with one adjective left out before way, which the solver supplies

explanation.surface: A line from Gray's Elegy about a tired farmhand trudging home.
explanation.walkthrough: A fill-in clue: the line reads 'The ploughman homeward plods his ___ way'; the missing word describes how tired he is.
explanation.definitionFit: The word Gray chose for the ploughman's tired, trudging path home completes the famous line.

clue.text: Where the lowest ranks may be accommodated?

definitions.text: Where the lowest ranks may be accommodated?

parts.words: Where the lowest ranks may be accommodated?
parts.note: the lowest army rank is the ordinary soldier, so a lodging for them sounds like a barrack, but the phrase names a small exclusive guesthouse

explanation.surface: Asking where the most junior soldiers are billeted.
explanation.definitionFit: A guesthouse that takes only selected residents, not the public, is so called; ordinary soldiers punningly suit it.

clue.text: Painter's underwear!

definitions.meaning: Sir Stanley Spencer, English painter of Cookham, with possessive
close-fitting woollen vests or bodices worn under clothes

explanation.surface: An artist's undergarments.
explanation.definitionFit: Stanley Spencer was an English painter; a spencer is also a short knitted undergarment.

clue.text: Put many, perhaps a thousand, in a drum

indicators.note: perhaps hints the letters of put many could be rearranged

parts.note: M is the Roman numeral for a thousand

explanation.surface: Squeezing lots, maybe a thousand, into a drum.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Perhaps' rearranges PUT MANY into TYMPANU, then M is added.
explanation.definitionFit: The tympanum is the eardrum, or a drum's stretched membrane, from the Greek for drum.

clue.text: A subject of interest in the main

definitions.text: A subject of interest in the main

parts.words: A subject of interest in the main
parts.note: in the main reads as mostly, but the main is also the sea, so this is a field of study concerned with the sea

explanation.surface: A topic that is chiefly of interest.
explanation.definitionFit: The science of seas studies the 'main', the old poetic word for the open sea.

clue.text: Beat the woman holding a medal

indicators.note: the word for the woman holds the medal inside it

parts.note: her refers to a woman
MM is the Military Medal

explanation.surface: Thrashing the woman who clutches a decoration.
explanation.definitionFit: To hammer someone is to pound or defeat them heavily.

clue.text: The good man in a rush appears relaxed

indicators.note: the saint is placed inside the rush

parts.note: a reed is a rush, the marsh plant
ST, saint, is the crossword's good man

explanation.surface: The saint who appears calm even in haste.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rush' looks like hurry; it is the marsh plant, a reed.
explanation.definitionFit: Rested means having taken a break, refreshed and relaxed.

clue.text: Assist a punt

parts.note: a punt is a gamble, a bet

explanation.surface: Helping someone with a small flutter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Punt' suggests a boat; in betting slang it is a wager.
explanation.definitionFit: To abet is to help or encourage, usually in wrongdoing.

clue.text: Move inside whatever is suffering

indicators.note: the word for move goes inside the other

parts.note: any means whatever, as in 'any one you like'
to go is to move

explanation.surface: Moving within whatever causes pain.
explanation.definitionFit: Agony is intense physical or mental pain.

clue.text: Poles having a quiet break

parts.note: S and N are the south and north poles
p, piano, means quietly in music

explanation.surface: Polish people enjoying a calm holiday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Poles' suggests people from Poland; it is the two magnetic poles.
explanation.definitionFit: To snap is to break suddenly and cleanly.

clue.text: A lot of sailors love this river

parts.note: RN is the Royal Navy
love is zero in tennis, the letter O

explanation.surface: Seamen are fond of this waterway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lot of' is padding for the surface; the pieces are A, RN and O.
explanation.definitionFit: The Arno is the Italian river flowing through Florence and Pisa.

clue.text: Gossip turning up with a lengthy tale

indicators.note: in a down clue turning up means the word reads from bottom to top

parts.note: gas is idle chatter

explanation.surface: Tittle-tattle arriving with a long story.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turning up' sends GAS upwards to SAG, then A follows.
explanation.definitionFit: A saga is a long story of heroic deeds or of a family's history.

clue.text: Stuff that's relevant

explanation.surface: Something that is pertinent.
explanation.definitionFit: Material means cloth or substance; it also means pertinent, as in a material witness.

clue.text: In short, aver none drink here

indicators.note: in tells us the letters sit within these words

explanation.surface: Briefly put, nobody would claim a drink here.
explanation.walkthrough: The run starts at the T ending 'short' and stops at the N of 'none'.
explanation.definitionFit: An inn or pub is a place where people drink.

clue.text: Soldiers once cadets or otherwise

explanation.surface: Young recruits, or else ex-soldiers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Otherwise' rearranges CADETS OR.
explanation.definitionFit: British soldiers wore scarlet tunics until the late nineteenth century, so were nicknamed after them.

clue.text: The cost of liberation

parts.note: the price paid to free someone, as from kidnappers

explanation.surface: What it costs to set someone free.
explanation.definitionFit: A sum demanded for releasing a captive is the price of their freedom.
